concepts.plainMeaning: An over-the-counter contract where two counterparties agree to lock an interest rate on a principal amount over a future period.
concepts.roleHere: Core derivative contract introduced in Section 4.7 for hedging interest rate risk.
concepts.analogy: Like signing a guaranteed fixed hotel rate months in advance of a peak holiday trip.

concepts.plainMeaning: The standard abbreviation for a Forward Rate Agreement contract.
concepts.roleHere: Used as the standard acronym across all formulas and pricing statements.
concepts.analogy: A financial short-hand acronym like ATM or APR.

concepts.plainMeaning: The hypothetical face amount used solely to calculate interest cash payments without ever being borrowed or lent.
concepts.roleHere: Defines the scale L of interest calculations in the FRA payoff formula.
concepts.analogy: An agreed insured property value used to calculate claim payouts without moving the building.

concepts.plainMeaning: Settling a financial agreement through a single net cash transfer at start date T1 instead of borrowing the full principal.
concepts.roleHere: Explains why the FRA payoff is discounted back to settlement date T1.
concepts.analogy: Settling a friendly bet with coins at the start of a match rather than exchanging expensive tickets.

concepts.plainMeaning: The weighted average time in years until all cash flow payments of a bond are received.
concepts.roleHere: Core metric in Section 4.8 measuring interest rate sensitivity and effective maturity.
concepts.analogy: The physical balance point on a seesaw where weighted coupon bricks balance out the fulcrum.

concepts.plainMeaning: Macaulay duration adjusted for compounding frequency, measuring percentage bond price change per unit yield shift.
concepts.roleHere: Provides the linear slope linking rate hikes directly to portfolio price declines.
concepts.analogy: A car steering ratio that shows how many degrees the tires pivot for every turn of the steering wheel.

concepts.plainMeaning: The curvature in a bond's price-yield curve showing how duration changes as interest rates shift.
concepts.roleHere: Provides the second-order Taylor correction in Section 4.9 for large interest rate moves.
concepts.analogy: A curved archery bow that bends stiffer and stiffer the harder you pull the string.

concepts.plainMeaning: The economic theory stating forward rates exceed expected future zero rates because lenders demand an extra premium for locking funds in long maturities.
concepts.roleHere: Explains why upward-sloping yield curves naturally dominate normal economic conditions in Section 4.10.
concepts.analogy: A landlord charging higher total rent for a ten-year fixed lease to give up liquidity.

concepts.plainMeaning: The economic theory stating long-term interest rates are simply an average of expected future short-term rates without risk premiums.
concepts.roleHere: Provides the foundational baseline hypothesis for the shape of the term structure of interest rates in Section 4.10.
concepts.analogy: Estimating the total travel time of a journey by simply averaging the speed limits of each individual road segment.

concepts.plainMeaning: Matching portfolio duration against interest rate futures contracts to neutralize price volatility from yield curve shifts.
concepts.roleHere: Introduces the duration-based hedging formula N* for bond portfolios in Section 4.8.
concepts.analogy: Placing counterbalancing sandbags on a balance beam to cancel out an uneven tilt.

concepts.plainMeaning: A landmark 1994 municipal bankruptcy where a leveraged repo portfolio collapsed after aggressive interest rate hikes.
concepts.roleHere: The real-world case study in Section 4.8 showing what happens when duration risk is ignored.
concepts.analogy: A speedboat loaded with heavy cargo that flips over when hitting unexpectedly tall waves.

concepts.plainMeaning: The interest rate implied today for borrowing or lending money across a future time period.
concepts.roleHere: The current market forward benchmark R_F used to calculate the value of an existing FRA.
concepts.analogy: A contract price agreed today for delivery of grain three months into the future.
